transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, what really brought me in is that I've been having some trouble keeping track of conversations. For example, my wife will be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or figuring out his rides, and I’m looking right at her while she's talking. But a minute later, I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. It happens enough that it's becoming an issue, so I figured I should come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you noticed any other difficulties with your memory or thinking, like forgetting recent events or struggling to find words during conversations?

No, not really. My memory itself seems to be fine. If I actually pay attention and hear what's going on, I remember it without a problem. And I don't struggle to find words when I'm talking, either. It's really just... well, it's just that issue of tuning out and not taking the information in to begin with.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or concentrating on tasks, like reading or following along with a TV show, where you lose track of what's happening?

Yeah, I do. Like, if I sit down to work out a catering order, or if I'm listening through a parish planning call... I usually start off fine. But before long, my mind just wanders off. I end up having to go back over the exact same notes, almost like I never even read them to begin with.
Have you been feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or experiencing any unusual thoughts or perceptions lately?
No, I wouldn't say that. I still enjoy the things I usually do, and my mood has been fine. It's really just the focus thing. No strange thoughts or anything like that, either.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with staying focused? Was it something that's been with you for a long time, maybe even since childhood, or is it more recent?

It's been there a long time, really. Even back in grade school, well before I was 12, my teachers would tell my parents that I was bright but always daydreaming. I was the kid who would leave my homework sitting in my desk, and I always needed reminders just to finish the work we were supposed to be doing in class. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing.
Do you experience these same difficulties with focus and attention in other settings, like at work, in meetings, or during social interactions outside of your family?

Well, I'm not working a regular job right now, so I don't really have that setting to judge by. And socially... I don't know, I haven't really noticed it being a problem when I'm just hanging out with friends or talking to neighbors. It really just seems to happen when I'm trying to sit down and focus on those specific tasks I mentioned before. So, no, I can't really say I've noticed it causing trouble in other areas.

Have you ever noticed these same kinds of focus problems in different situations, like when you're having a conversation with someone one-on-one, or when you're reading something for pleasure, or maybe when you were in school listening to a lecture or trying to study?

Well, like I said, I haven't really noticed it in conversations or anything like that. When I'm talking to someone, I'm usually fine. And reading for pleasure... I don't read a whole lot, to be honest, but when I do, it's usually something I'm interested in, so it's not a big issue. Back in school, yeah, maybe a bit during lectures, but right now, it's really just those specific tasks at home I told you about. It doesn't seem to happen across the board.

Can you think of any other situations, even small ones, where you've had trouble focusing—like when you're listening to directions, managing your schedule, or following along with something that requires a bit of mental effort, even for a short time?

Well, I guess... if I think about it, there are a few other things. Like if I sit down to work out a catering order, or if I'm listening through one of those parish planning calls. I usually start off fine, you know? But before long, my mind just wanders off. Then I end up having to go back over the same notes, and it's like I never even read them the first time. So I suppose it does happen with things that take a bit of mental effort like that.

Do you have trouble focusing in any other situations, even ones we haven’t talked about yet—like when you're listening to someone give directions, managing your schedule, or doing something that takes even a little bit of mental focus?

No, honestly, I think we've covered it. Aside from the catering orders and those parish calls I just mentioned, I really can't think of anything else. My schedule isn't too complicated these days, and I don't really have issues with directions or anything like that. It just seems to be those specific things where I have to really sit and think.
Have these difficulties with focusing caused any problems in your life, like missed deadlines, mistakes at work, or issues with relationships because you seemed distracted or not listening?

Well, it has caused a few issues, yeah. Mostly at home. It's started causing some tension with my wife, honestly. She feels like she can't really count on me when it comes to helping out with my cousin's care, which... well, that's hard to hear, but I get it. And with the catering stuff, I've had to go back and double-check things or even redo some tasks just to make sure those small jobs don't get mixed up. So, it is definitely getting in the way a bit.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, or lost interest in most things for two weeks or longer?

No, I can't say that I have. I mean, sure, I get frustrated sometimes with the things we've been talking about, but I wouldn't say I've ever felt really down or depressed like that. And I still enjoy doing the things I usually do. So, no, nothing like that for two weeks or anything.

Looking back, do you think these focus issues have been present across most areas of your life, even when you were in school or doing other activities that required attention, or have they mostly been limited to specific tasks like the ones you mentioned?

Well, yeah, looking back... it really has been an issue for a long time. Even back in grade school, you know, before I was 12, I remember my teachers telling my parents that I was a bright kid, but I was just always daydreaming. I would leave my homework sitting in my desk, and I always needed reminders to actually finish my classwork. So, it's definitely not just a recent thing.

Can you recall if you've had trouble focusing during other types of tasks, even ones that aren't related to parish calls or catering orders—like conversations, reading, or even just listening to someone give you information that you need to act on?

Yeah, conversations are definitely an issue. In fact, that's what really brought me in here. My wife will be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or his rides, and I’m looking right at her while she speaks... but a minute later, I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said.

Do you find it hard to stay focused when you're reading something that requires a bit of mental effort, like news articles or detailed instructions, or when you're listening to someone explain something complex?

Yes, definitely. Like, if I sit down to work out the details for a catering order, or if I'm listening in on one of those parish planning calls... I'll start off fine. I'm paying attention. But before long, my mind just wanders off. I end up having to go back over the same notes or information again, almost like I never read them in the first place.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated during situations where it’s expected, like during meetings or other quiet activities?

No, not really. I don't have much trouble sitting still. If I need to sit through a meeting or just be quiet at home, I can stay in my chair fine. It's more that my mind is wandering off, not my body. I don't really get fidgety or feel the need to get up and pace around or anything like that.

No features of depression, anxiety, or stress-related disorders were endorsed to justify F32.9, F33.9, or F43.10. The symptom pattern is most consistent with F90.0 (ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation).

opening_question.intent: Establish the patient's primary concern or reason for seeking evaluation.
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a long-standing pattern of inattention beginning before age 12, persisting into adulthood, and causing functional impairment in task completion and interpersonal relationships. There is no evidence of hyperactivity, mood disturbance, or anxiety sufficient to meet criteria for alternative diagnoses.
